newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends near lows, seen weakening.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends near lows, seen weakening.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended a volatile session near the day's lows on continued, technically-driven speculative liquidation, dealers said.
The action pushed most-active March contract to a low of 11.19, where a double-bottom has formed on the charts, but the trade proved to be a steady buyer at the lows.
"A lot of contracts changed hands at lower levels," a dealer said, noting today's volume, estimated at a brisk 32,653 lots.
Still, open interest remains high and traders said the speculators could have more positions to liquidate.
"It's not over yet," one trader warned. "There is still a lot of buying the funds and specs did at much lower levels, and they're hoping for a rally."
But today's close near the lows may signal continued weakness, dealers said, citing possible sell stops below today's low of 11.19. Support in March was pegged between 11.15 and 11.10.
The most-active March contract ended off 0.16 at 11.21, having ranged from 11.37 to 11.19. Spot-October slid 0.23 on the day to 11.19, while the deferred contracts finished 0.10 to 0.06 weaker.
March closed at a 0.02 cent premium to October, compared with a discount of 0.05 on Thursday's close.
LIFFE white sugar futures also closed sharply lower, with the spot-December contract off $3.10 to $328.50. The back months settled $3.00 to 90 cents weaker.
